transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-21
- Time: 10:00 PDT / 18:00Z
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Martinez (Redwood SE); Priya Kapoor (SprigLab CTO); Alex Nguyen (SprigLab Lead Platform Eng); Samir Patel (SprigLab Security); Lena Ortiz (Product)
transcript_body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we can see people on the call. Quick intro round — I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood Inference team.
[00:18] Alex: Hi, Alex here — lead on the platform side at SprigLab.
[00:24] Priya: Priya, CTO, we'll be owning the project timeline.
[00:30] Diego (SE): Diego from Redwood, I run the integration POCs.
[00:36] Samir: Samir, security lead.
[00:40] Lena: Lena, product.
[00:45] Maya: Cool. High level: SprigLab is evaluating three deployment modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). Today we want to focus on integration flow: SDK usage, LangChain/LlamaIndex compatibility, gateway/proxy model routing, rate limits, and observability hooks. Does that sound right?
[01:05] Priya: Yes, that's it. We also want to understand what parts of our stack change for each mode, right — like networking and auth.
[01:12] Maya: Exactly. Diego, do you want to run through the SDK and LangChain bits?
[01:18] Diego: Sure. So Redwood provides language SDKs in Python and Node; the client is a thin wrapper over the REST streaming endpoints. For LangChain integration you can use the Redwood LLM wrapper which maps to the generate/chat endpoints. There's also a connector for LlamaIndex — a small adapter that handles document stores and embeddings.
[01:38] Alex: Quick question — do the SDKs surface prefix/KV cache control? We do a lot of long-running chat sessions and want to reuse KV caches across requests.
[01:46] Diego: Good question. The runtime exposes a session token and a cache key. The SDK has helpers — you can set cache_scope and keep-alive TTL on the session. I will say sometimes the auto-transcription of our docs calls the KV cache "Kay-Vee" which is confusing, but yes, control exists. For Dedicated you can pin a cache to a GPU pool for affinity; for Hosted you get prefix-caching but not guaranteed pinning.
[02:13] Priya: So if we go Dedicated, we can ensure lower variance in latency for those long chats?
[02:18] Diego: Exactly. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and more deterministic throughput; it also supports cache pinning and burst capacity options. Hosted is simpler to get started and has backoff fallback to smaller models.
[02:30] Samir: From security: For Private we need KMS integration and audit logs to satisfy our compliance. How does Redwood handle key management and logs?
[02:39] Maya: For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — you manage keys, Redwood supports envelope encryption. Audit logs are delivered to S3 or your SIEM via syslog. We'll send the SOC2 pack.
[02:50] Samir: Do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC for the control plane?
[02:55] Diego: Yes, SAML and OIDC for SSO, and granular RBAC for model secrets and rollouts. In Private the control plane can be customer-managed so access boundaries are tight.
[03:05] Lena: On the SDK side, we use LangChain extensively. Are there prebuilt chains or examples for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that tie to your embeddings API?
[03:13] Diego: Yes, we have a LangChain connector that demonstrates retrieval + generation, and a LlamaIndex example repo for chunking and indexing. I will share a repo link. The embeddings endpoint uses consistent vector dimensions across models in the catalog; for Dedicated you can choose different embedding variants.
[03:29] Alex: How does the gateway/proxy pattern work? We have an internal API gateway and would like to route requests to different models or to fallback endpoints based on rate limits or latency SLOs.
[03:38] Maya: Redwood supports a gateway layer that you can run as a sidecar or as a centralized proxy. The gateway can route by policy — model, region, or tier. It also emits request traces and spans that map back to the Redwood request id for end-to-end observability.
[03:52] Diego: To add, the proxy can implement token bucket rate limits and per-customer quotas. It also has a built-in policy engine so you can do A/B routing — e.g., 10% to a smaller quantized model for cost control, automatically fall back to a larger one on quality regressions.
[04:10] Priya: That policy engine — is it declarative? Where do we configure it?
[04:15] Diego: It's config-driven YAML that sits next to the proxy. You can also manage it via the Redwood Console — rollout rules, canaries, and percentage splits.
[04:25] Samir: Our security team will want to ensure the proxy isn't a single point of failure and that logs are scrubbed of PII before leaving the app.
[04:33] Maya: Good note. The proxy supports local scrubbing hooks and can push logs to your logging endpoint. We can ship sample middleware for PII redaction.
[04:42] Alex: About rate limits — what granularity? Per API key, per route, per model?
[04:47] Diego: All of the above. Rate limits can be applied at API key, route, and model granularity, with adjustable windows and burst sizes. For Dedicated you get higher baseline throughput and more lenient quotas by contract.
[04:58] Lena: For observability, do you support OpenTelemetry traces? We want to tie token-level latencies to our traces.
[05:04] Diego: Yes, OpenTelemetry is supported. The SDK emits spans for request start, first token, and completion. The Console aggregates token-level cost and latency as well, and you can ingest traces into your APM.
[05:18] Priya: We also need to run regression tests against prompt sets — can Redwood integrate with our eval pipelines?
[05:25] Maya: Redwood Optimize has an eval integration — you feed prompt sets and metrics; it will alert on quality regressions and suggest quantization or model swaps. For initial POC we can wire your evals to the staging endpoint.
[05:36] Alex: One of our constraints is bursty traffic with sustained periods of low usage. We want to avoid paying for steady capacity but still hit SLOs during spikes. Thoughts?
[05:45] Diego: Two patterns: use Hosted with burst credits and fallback models, or Dedicated with autoscale/burst policies. Dedicated with a burst pool is often the middle ground — reserve baseline and pay for bursts. We can show cost math.
[05:58] Priya: What about data residency? We have EMEA customers; do you have region pinning?
[06:04] Maya: Yes. Hosted supports region pinning for model execution and storage. Private gives you full control for on-prem. Dedicated can be provisioned in specified cloud regions.
[06:12] Samir: We need to see audit log format — ideally event types, timestamps, user ids, request ids.
[06:18] Diego: We'll send a sample log export.
[06:21] Maya: Quick clarification on the PII redaction — do you want an SDK-level hook or the proxy-level redaction?
[06:27] Samir: Both would be ideal, but proxy-level is minimal change for us.
[06:31] Diego: We'll include a proxy middleware pattern that you can drop in.
[06:36] [07:00] Maya: Do you have any hard blockers for moving forward?
[07:04] Priya: Main blockers: security review timeline, cost/commit decisions, and a small set of performance numbers for our chat profile.
[07:12] Alex: We'll need an example of LangChain usage where the model is switched mid-flow — like switch to a smaller model for certain intents.
[07:20] Diego: That's supported by the proxy policy — we'll include a sample policy and LangChain snippet that triggers model swap by intent tag.
[07:28] Lena: Any concerns around prompt leakage between customer sessions?
[07:33] Diego: Requests are tenant-isolated by default; KV caches are scoped per-tenant unless you explicitly share.
[07:40] Priya: For the POC, what would you recommend we test first?
[07:44] Maya: Two things: 1) Functional integration — LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters and SDK calls; 2) Performance — a 48-hour burst profile with typical chat flows and token distribution. We can provision Dedicated trial capacity for that.
[07:58] Alex: That sounds right. We'll need to confirm stakeholders and exact traffic pattern.
[08:04] Samir: On compliance, we'll need to run vulnerability scans against the on-prem bundle. Is that allowed?
[08:09] Diego: Yes, we provide a vendor bundle for on-prem and allow scans under NDA.
[08:15] [09:00] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send pricing, SOC2/ISO pack, LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repos, proxy middleware examples, and sample log schema. SprigLab to confirm internal reviewers and pick POC dates.
[09:15] Priya: We'll target a POC kickoff the week of April 6th.
[09:20] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[09:24] Lena: Can you also include a minimal terraform snippet for Dedicated provisioning?
[09:28] Diego: Yup — I'll add that to the repo.
[09:32] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:35] Alex: Thanks, bye.
[09:37] Priya: Thanks.
[09:40] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions for technical names (e.g., Kay-Vee for KV), speaker overlaps near Q&A.
